- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.2) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 3–8% to match true decline.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–7 days; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.0 or vice versa), model reacts with lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment shift.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; add 1–2% lagged momentum to forecast.
